title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs (quatrième mouture)' develops a purely combinatorial model of tame one-dimensional topology. The elementary cells are points P_a and open segments S_ab (a<b) on an ordered 'line' L. 'Figures' and 'préfigures' are sets of such cells. Supports are defined by a polarity (Galois connection) built from a separation relation |∘|:
- cosupp°(Φ) = {Z' : Z' |∘| Φ}.
- supp°(Φ) = {Z : Z |∘| Z' for all Z' ∈ cosupp°(Φ)}, i.e. the bipolar closure of Φ.
- Omb (ombre, 'shadow') is the explicit set of cells contained in a cell's closure; Omb° is the analogous set of cells under the 'open' ordering.
- For cells, the page reads Z |∘| X as 'Z ≤_pos X or Z ≥_pos X': one cell lies entirely to one side of the other.

The page first states the general case (b) of the computation begun on the previous page. Let T be a polygonal (in Dev*(L)) with origin a and extremity b, let α ⊂ ∂T={a,b}, let β be its complement in ∂T, and let Φ_{T,α} = F_T \ α. Then supp Φ_{T,α} = Omb(S̃_ab) \ α = Omb°(S_ab) ∪ β, a disjoint union. In words, the closure-type support of the polygonal 'segment with some endpoints removed' is the full interval shadow minus the removed endpoints. Case (a), the irreducible case, is already done; parts (v) and (b) remain.

To prove (v), Grothendieck reduces by induction on the number of connected components to a Lemma.
- Hypothesis: X ∈ M and Φ, Ψ ⊂ M (perhaps polygonals) with Φ <_pos X <_pos Ψ.
- Conclusion: supp°(Φ ∪ Ψ) = supp°(Φ) ∪ supp°(Ψ).
- NB: for polygonals, such a separating cell X exists iff Φ <^1 Ψ. If ex δΦ = a < or δΨ = b, take X = S_ab; if a = b, take X = P_a.

This is an additivity statement for the bipolar closure operator. Such closures are not additive on unions in general, but they are on position-separated pieces, a combinatorial analogue of closure commuting with finite unions.

Proof begun on the page:
1. The inclusion ⊇ is clear by monotonicity.
2. For ⊆: since Φ <_pos X <_pos Ψ, X is separated from every cell of Φ ∪ Ψ, so X ∈ cosupp°(Φ ∪ Ψ).
3. Hence any Z ∈ supp°(Φ ∪ Ψ) satisfies Z |∘| X, i.e. Z ≤_pos X or Z ≥_pos X.
4. The next page proves Z < X ⇒ Z ∈ supp°Φ and Z > X ⇒ Z ∈ supp°Ψ, by case analysis on the separating cell (P_a or S_ab).

The purpose is to compute supports of polygonal figures component by component in this combinatorial tame-topology framework.
errors: No real errors. The lemma's hypotheses are left uncertain: the margin note 'Voir s'il faut supposer Φ, Ψ des polygonales' shows Grothendieck himself was unsure whether polygonality is needed.
The NB's equivalence 'existence of X ⇔ Φ <^1 Ψ' is only asserted for polygonals and relies on the definitions of ex δ, or δ and <^1 given earlier. It is plausible but not checked on this page.

The statement Z |∘| X ⇔ Z ≤_pos X or Z ≥_pos X is used as a definition-level fact for single cells. The case Z = X (e.g. X = P_a) must be excluded by irreflexivity of |∘|; the next page treats the P_a case separately.

ideas.what: Support/closure of a set of cells defined as a bipolar (polarity) closure with respect to a 'positional separation' relation |∘| on cells of a combinatorial line
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity closure operator (formal concept analysis style); combinatorial model of tame (o-minimal-like) topology of the line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); tame topology programme announced by Grothendieck, o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only announces 'topologie modérée'; this combinatorial support formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Additivity lemma: supp° of a union of two pieces separated by an intermediate cell equals the union of their supp°
ideas.modern_name: additivity of a closure operator on separated sets (analogue of the Kuratowski axiom cl(A∪B)=cl A ∪ cl B)

ideas.what: Explicit computation of the support of a polygonal minus endpoints: Omb(S̃_ab)\α = Omb°(S_ab) ∪ β
ideas.modern_name: closure of a half-open interval in an ordered cell complex

missed.claim: The page documents Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to found 'analysis situs' on a polarity (bipolar closure) between cells and a separation relation, rather than on open sets. It is part of an unpublished, little-studied combinatorial tame-topology formalism, but this particular page contains only a routine lemma within that framework.
missed.quote: Alors supp°(Φ ∪ Ψ) = supp°(Φ) ∪ supp°(Ψ) ... Voir s'il faut supposer Φ, Ψ des polygonales.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest for reconstructing what 'topologie modérée' meant concretely to Grothendieck. It is a possible point of comparison with o-minimal cell decomposition and with closure-space / formal-concept approaches, but it holds no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step, an additivity lemma for a polarity-defined support, inside an unpublished combinatorial model of the line. The framework itself is little-known, but the mathematics on this page is elementary and routine.
transcription_corrections: 'par réc. sur ↯[?] nb de composantes connexes' should read 'par réc. sur le nb de composantes connexes'.
In the NB, 'ex δΦ [-=-] = a' has an overwritten/struck '=' before '= a'; the intended reading is 'si ex δΦ = a < or δΨ = b, on prend X = S_ab'.
The final line reads 'donc Z |∘| X, ce qui signifie : ou bien Z ≤_pos X ou Z ≥_pos X', with the pos subscripts under both inequalities.
The margin note reads 'Voir s'il faut supposer Φ, Ψ des polygonales.'
